translations.text: Love righteousness, you judges of the earth. Think about the Lord with good thoughts, and seek him with a sincere heart.
For he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and he reveals himself to those who trust in him.
For evil thoughts lead away from God, but the power that tests rebukes fools.
For wisdom does not enter a soul entangled in evil, nor does it dwell in a body enslaved to sin.
For the holy spirit and discipline flee from deceit, keep far from the thoughts of those who lack knowledge, and rebuke every injustice that comes.

For the spirit of wisdom loves human beings, but it does not acquit a blasphemous people of what their lips have said, because God witnesses their innermost motives, truly examines the heart, and hears the human tongue.
For the spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and the one who holds everything together knows its voice.
Therefore no one who speaks unjustly remains hidden, nor will that person escape a judgment of condemnation.
For the thoughts of the wicked person will be investigated, and a report of his words will come before the Lord to expose his wickedness.
For the jealous ear hears everything, and the whisper of grumbling is not hidden.
Therefore beware of useless grumbling, and spare your tongues from slander, because secret speech does not pass without consequences, and a lying mouth kills the soul.
Do not covet death through the errors of your life, and do not let yourselves be swept away into ruin by the destructive work of your hands.
For God did not make death, nor does he desire the destruction of the living.
Rather, he created everything to exist, and the offspring of the world have life. There is no deadly poison in them, nor does Sheol have dominion over the earth.
For righteousness is immortal.
But the wicked summoned him by their words and deeds. They considered him their friend and wasted away. They swore and made a covenant with him, because they were worthy to belong to his portion.
For they said to themselves, without thinking rightly: Our life is short and full of distress. There is no remedy when a person departs, and no one has been known to escape from Sheol.
For we came into being suddenly, and afterward we return to being as though we had never existed. For the breath in our nostrils is like smoke, and speech stirs like a spark in our heart.
When it is extinguished, the body becomes like ashes, and the spirit disperses like thin air.
Our name is forgotten after a time, and no one remembers our deeds. Our life passes like the traces of clouds and like mist driven away by the sun’s rays and weighed down by its heat.
For our life is a passing shadow, and there is no remedy at our departure, because it has been sealed, and no one can turn it back.
Come, then, let us enjoy these good things, and eagerly make use of these created things while we are young.
Let us fill ourselves with choice wine and perfumes, and let the [?] of the air not pass us by.
Let us crown ourselves with rose blossoms before they wither.
Let none of us go without pleasure, even into our old age. Let us leave traces of our pleasure everywhere, because this is our portion and this is our inheritance.
Let us overpower the righteous poor person. Let us have no pity on the widow or the orphan, and let us show no respect for an old man advanced in years.
Let our strength be our law of righteousness, because the weak are condemned as feeble.
Let us trouble the righteous person, because he displeases us. He opposes our deeds, reproaches us with the deeds required by the law, and brings up against us the offenses of our insolence.
He claims to have knowledge of God and says of himself, “I am God’s son.”
He has become a reproach to our thoughts; even seeing him is a burden to us.
For his way of life is unlike other people’s, and his paths are different.
He considers us unclean and keeps away from our ways as though from impurity. He calls the ways and the final end of the righteous blessed, and boasts that God is his father.
Let us see whether his words are true; let us test him at his departure.
For if the righteous person is God’s son, God will receive him and rescue him from the hands of those who have risen against him.
Let us question him with insults and torture, so that we may learn how firmly he holds to his humility, and test whether there is evil in him.
Let us condemn him to a disgraceful death, for, according to his words, there will be an inquiry concerning him.
The foolish thought these things and went astray, because their wickedness blinded them.
They did not know God’s mysteries, did not hope for a holy reward, and did not value the souls of blameless elders.
For God created humanity to be free from decay; humanity was formed in the image of his likeness.
Through the devil’s envy, death entered the world, and those who belong to him experience it.
But the souls of the righteous are in God’s hands, and torment does not come near them.
In the eyes of fools they seemed to be dead, and their departure was considered a misfortune.
Their departure from us was regarded as destruction, but they are at peace.
For even if they are condemned in the eyes of human beings, their hope is full of life.
For he tested them a little, and they were disciplined a little, but they will inherit much, because God tested them and found them worthy of him.
He tested them like gold in a furnace and accepted them like burnt offerings and sacrifices of well-being.
In due time their examination will take place, and the righteous will run among the wicked like sparks among reeds.
The peoples will rejoice, the nations will be glad, and the Lord will reign over them forever.
Those who trust in him understand the truth, and those who are faithful remain devoted to him in love, because he gives grace and mercy to his chosen ones, and his care is over his holy ones.
But the wicked will receive disgrace in keeping with their thoughts—those who despised the Lord and withdrew from his righteous ones.
For whoever despises wisdom and discipline is miserable, and his hope is empty. Their labor lacks knowledge, and their deeds do not prosper.
Their wives are unwise, their children are wicked, and their offspring are cursed.
For it is well with the barren woman who has not defiled herself, who has not known a bed that leads to ruin. She will receive fruit when souls are visited.

And the eunuch whose hands have committed no lawlessness and who has devised no evil against the Lord will be given, for his goodness and faithfulness, a special favor and a desirable inheritance in the Lord’s house.
There is a choice reward for good toil, and the roots of chastity will not be uprooted.
The children of adulterers will not reach maturity, and offspring from an unlawful bed will be destroyed.
Even if they live long, they will be counted as nothing, and their old age will end in dishonor.
If they die prematurely, they have no hope and no comfort on the appointed day.
For the offspring of the wicked have a bitter end.
It is better to be childless with honor, for there is life in its remembrance, because it is known both to God and to human beings.

While she is present, they imitate her, and when she has departed, they long for her. In this world she wears adornment and a crown, and she is shown to have won the contest of those who are without blemish.
But the numerous offspring of the wicked are of no use, and those who come from foreign seed will not put down deep roots or have a secure foundation.
Even if they put out shoots and branches, they will flourish only for a time and will not develop securely. They will be shaken by the wind and uprooted by a strong wind.
Their branches will finally be broken off, and their fruit will be spoiled, unfit to eat and good for nothing.
Children born from unlawful intercourse are witnesses against their parents' wickedness when their parents are called to account.
But even if a righteous person dies suddenly, he will be at rest; and if he dies after a long life, he will be found in honor.
Old age and honor do not come from a long span of time, nor are they measured by the number of years.
Rather, a person's understanding is his gray hair, and a peaceful life is the full stature of old age.
Because he pleased God, he was loved; because he was living among sinners, God removed him.
He was snatched away so that evil would not change his thinking and deceit would not lead his tongue astray.
For evil zeal ruins good things, and the turmoil of desire corrupts a good mind.
Having been perfected in a short time, he fulfilled a long span of time.

For his soul pleased God, and because he was upright, God quickly took him away from the midst of wickedness. The peoples saw this but did not understand, nor did they consider why God had judged him in this way.
God's grace and mercy are among his holy ones, and God's care is over his chosen ones.
He judges the righteous and destroys the wicked while they are still alive. The short time of youths who depart is better than the long lives of deceitful old men.
For they will see the death of the righteous person but will not understand what God planned for him or why the Lord cared for him.
They will see him and despise him, but the Lord himself will laugh at them.

After these things they will become a shameful ruin and an everlasting disgrace among the dead. For saws will tear them apart without a sound, and they will be shaken from their foundations. They will be utterly laid waste and brought to destruction, and their memory will perish.
Deceit will enter their thoughts about their foolish deeds, and their waywardness will rebuke them openly, before their eyes.
Then the righteous person will stand with great confidence before those who oppressed him and those who denied him the reward of his labor.
For they will see him and be seized with great fear, and they will be astonished when they see his glory.
They will speak among themselves in remorse, groaning in anguish of spirit, and will say, “This is the one who was then an object of laughter and disgrace to us, and a byword for fools.”
We considered his life foolish and his death disgraceful.
How has he been counted among the children of God, and how is his inheritance among the holy ones?
“So we strayed from the way of truth. The light of righteousness did not shine on us, and the sun did not rise for us.
Our paths were filled with sins and destruction. We traveled through an untrodden wilderness and did not know the way of the Lord.
What benefit did our arrogance bring us? Or what did our arrogant way of life gain us?
For it passed like a shadow. What did our arrogant way of life gain us? All these things passed like shadows and like news that travels swiftly,
and like a ship passing over the waves of the sea: once it has passed, neither its tracks nor its course through the paths of the waves can be recognized.

Or like a bird flying through the air, whose track cannot be traced: it beats its wings, stirs and parts the light wind, and cuts through the air with its powerful pinions. It travels by the beating of its wings, but afterward its passage cannot be recognized, and no one can find a sign of its route.
Or like an arrow shot at a target: it pierces the air, and immediately the air returns to its place, and its path cannot be recognized.”
So we too were born and came to an end. We could show no sign of goodness, but were overwhelmed by our wicked deeds.”
For the hope of the wicked is like sand carried away by the wind, like chaff carried away by a whirlwind, like smoke scattered by the wind, and like the memory of a traveler's day. So we passed away.
But the righteous live forever. Their reward is with the Lord, and their thoughts are with the Most High.
Therefore they will receive a glorious kingdom and a beautiful crown from the Lord's hand. With his right hand he shelters them, and with his arm he shields them.
For their sake, in his zeal, he will arm everything, and he will arm all his creation alongside him for war against his enemies.
He will put on righteousness as a breastplate and place on his head a helmet of judgment without falsehood.
He will take holiness as an invincible shield.
He will sharpen the sword of his anger wondrously, and the people of the world will wage war alongside him against fools.
Arrows of flashes and lightning will pass over them. As at a target, they will be released from the curved bow of the clouds.
In wrath he will hurl hailstones at them like rocks. The waters of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will violently overwhelm them.
A terrible wind will rise against them and scatter them like a whirlwind. It will devastate the whole land of the wicked and crush the evildoers, the dominion of the powerful, and their thrones.
Listen, therefore, you kings, and understand; learn, you judges of the ends of the earth.
Pay attention, you who rule over many and boast of the multitudes of nations.
For your dominion was given to you by the Lord, and your strength comes from the Most High. He examines your deeds and searches your thoughts.
For although you were servants of his kingdom, you did not judge rightly, keep his law, or conduct yourselves according to God's purposes.
He will rise against you terribly and swiftly, for a terrible judgment will come upon those in high positions.
For a humble king is close to mercy, but the powerful will be called to account powerfully.
For the Lord of all shows no partiality and is not intimidated by greatness, because he made both the great and the small and cares equally for everyone.
And he examines the mighty in truth.
My words are addressed to you, rulers, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall.
For those who love holiness will be made holy in holiness, and those who learn it will find beauty.
Therefore desire my words and love them, and you will be instructed.
Wisdom is radiant and does not decay. She is easily seen by those who love her and is discovered by those who seek her.
And she reveals herself to those who long to seek her.
Whoever comes to her early will not grow weary, for he will readily find her standing at his door.
For to reflect on her is perfect wisdom, and those who keep watch for her will soon be free from anxiety.
For she comes to visit those who are worthy of her. She appears to them on their paths continually and meets them in every thought.
For the beginning of desire for her is truth and instruction.
Meditation on instruction is love, and love is the keeping of her law. Understanding her law is assurance that does not decay.
And deeds free from corruption bring people near to God.
For desire for wisdom leads up to kingship.
If you desire thrones and royal scepters, you rulers of the people, honor wisdom so that you may reign forever.

I will explain what wisdom is and how she came to be, and I will not hide mysteries from you. I will trace what came before creation and openly set out the knowledge of her, and I will not depart from the truth.
And I will not walk in envy, because it has no fellowship with wisdom.
A multitude of wise people is the life of the world, and a wise king sustains the people.
Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will inherit life.
For I too am a mortal human being, like everyone else, a descendant of the first man, who was born of the earth. In my mother's womb I was formed into flesh.
For a period of ten months I took shape in blood, from a man's seed and from the desire of sleeping together.
When I was born, I broke through into the air shared by all and fell upon the earth like everyone else. Like everyone else, I began my first utterance with crying.
And I was carefully wrapped in swaddling clothes.
For no king or ruler has ever had a different kind of birth.
For everyone has one entrance into the world, and likewise one departure.
Because of this I prayed, and a spirit of wisdom was given to me. I called out, and a spirit of knowledge came to me.
I desired her more than scepters and thrones, and I did not consider wealth comparable to her.
I did not compare her to a precious stone, because all gold before her is like a little dust, and silver is regarded as mud before her.
I loved her more than beauty and health. I chose her over light, because wisdom's own light never sleeps.
All good things came to me together with her, and immeasurable wealth was in her hands.
I delighted in all these things because wisdom guides them, though I did not know that she came before them all.
I learned without deceit, and I give without envy; I will not hide her wealth from you.
For she is an inexhaustible treasure for humanity. Those who acquired her entered into friendship with God, because they stood firm in instruction that protects.
May God grant me to speak with sound judgment and to think appropriately about what is said, because he is the guide of wisdom, and he directs the wise.
In his hand are we and our words, all wisdom and knowledge and deeds.
For he gave me knowledge free from falsehood, to understand how the world is constituted and how the elements work.
The beginning, end, and middle of times, the changes of things, and how times pass;
The course of the years and the arrangement of the stars.
The nature of livestock and the fury of wild animals, the force of winds and the thoughts of human beings, the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.
I learned everything hidden and everything revealed.

For wisdom, who is skilled in everything, taught me. In her there is a spirit of knowledge, holy, unique, subtle, having many parts, moving readily, clear in voice, undefiled, wise and reliable, unyielding, loving good things, discerning, free from deceit, and beneficial.

She loves humanity, is strong, steadfast, and free from anxiety. She is mighty and able to do everything, and she attends to everything. She is intelligent and pure, embraces all spirits, and is subtle and radiant.
Wisdom moves and acts in every movement; she is the one who holds sway above [?] because of her purity.
She is the breath of God's power and stands in the glory of God, who holds all things. She is without falsehood; therefore nothing defiled enters her.
Wisdom is the radiance of light and does not decay. She is a mirror of glory for all God's works and an image of his goodness.
She is one, yet she can do everything. She endures, and everything is renewed through her. In every generation she brings peace to the souls of the faithful and forms friends of God and prophets.
For God loves only those in whom wisdom dwells.
For she is more beautiful than the sun and surpasses the entire array of stars. She was compared with light and was found to excel it.
After it comes night, but evil does not rule over wisdom.
For she extends herself firmly from one end to the other and deals gently with everything.
I loved her and sought her from my youth. I wanted to make her my bride, because I longed for her beauty.
There is joy and praise of God in companionship with her, because God is her Father, and the Lord of all loves her.
For she is God’s confidante, his partner in counsel, and the glory of all his works.
If wealth is desirable among the world’s possessions, what is richer than wisdom, who made everything?
If someone seeks skill for his work, who is more skilled than she?
If anyone loves righteousness, it is wonderful with her. For wisdom teaches self-control, righteousness, and courage. There is nothing in the world better for human beings than she is.

If anyone wishes to have great knowledge, she knows the things of the past and reveals what is to come. She knows the turns of speech and the solutions to hidden things. She knows signs and wonders beforehand, and the outcomes of times and seasons.
I chose her as my companion, knowing that she would be my counselor in good things and would remove anxiety and distress from me.
She brought me praise among many peoples and honor from elders in my youth.
She made me discerning in judgments and admired in the presence of powerful men.
When I am silent, they wait for me; when I open my mouth, they look at me; and when I speak at length, they put their hands over their mouths.
Because of her I will not die, and I will leave an everlasting remembrance to those who come after me.
I will govern peoples, and nations will be subject to me.
Tyrants will hear and be afraid, and they will be severely disciplined. Among the multitudes I am well regarded, and in battle I am a mighty warrior.
When I enter my house, I find rest with wisdom, for there is no bitterness in her dealings and no harm in her companionship, but delight and joy.
I considered these things within myself and reflected in my heart that there is life in intimacy with wisdom,

There is great delight in friendship with her, inexhaustible wealth in the labor of her hands, knowledge and beauty in studying her words, and unfailing truth in sharing her thoughts. I went about seeking to take her for myself.
I was a bright child, and I received a good soul.
Because of my goodness, I entered an undefiled body.

But I knew that I could not master myself unless God granted it to me—and this is enlightenment: to know from whom grace comes. I asked the Lord and pleaded with him, and with all my heart I said to him:
God of my ancestors and Lord of mercies, you made everything by your word,
and by your wisdom you formed humankind to have dominion over the creatures you made,
to govern the creation of the world in truth and righteousness, and to administer judgment with an upright soul.
Give me wisdom from before your throne, and do not reject me from among your servants.
For I am your servant, I am your servant and the son of your maidservant, a weak and short-lived man, lacking understanding of judgment and law.
For even if someone is perfect among human beings, when the spirit that comes from you departs from him, he is counted as nothing.
You are the one who chose me as king to rule your people and as judge over your sons and daughters.
You said that I should build a temple on your holy mountain and an altar in the city where you dwell, a likeness of your holy tabernacle, which you prepared long ago.
With you is wisdom, who knows your works. She was with you when you made the worlds, and she knows what is pleasing in your eyes and what is right according to your commandments.
Send her from your holy heavens, and send her from the throne of your majesty, so that she may come and labor with me, and I may know what is pleasing to you.
For she knows and understands everything. She will guide me wisely in all my deeds and guard me by her glory.
Then all my deeds will be acceptable, and I will be worthy of my father's throne.
For what human being knows God's counsel? Or who can work out what the Lord wills?
For the thoughts of mortals are weak, and their plans are uncertain.
For the perishable body weighs heavily on the soul.
Look, we barely comprehend the things on earth. We discover what is before our eyes with labor, and what is in our hands with toil. But who can investigate the things in heaven?
Who has known your counsel unless you gave wisdom and sent your Holy Spirit from your heavens?
In this way the paths on earth were made straight, human beings learned your will, and they lived through your wisdom.
She is the one who protected the first father, who was created alone in the world, and rescued him from his own fall.
She gave him strength to rule over everything.
But Cain the wrongdoer turned away from her, and anger destroyed him for killing his brother.
When the flood came upon the earth, Wisdom again saved life: she guided righteous Noah in a vessel of hewn wood.

When the members of the clans joined together in evil and were scattered, wisdom recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God. She also powerfully protected Abraham in the matter of his beloved son.
When the wicked perished, she rescued righteous Lot, who fled as fire came down upon the five cities.

The evidence of the wickedness of these places still stands to this day: they are smoking and desolate, the trees within them bear no fruit, and the person who did not believe became a pillar of salt.

For they disregarded wisdom and were not gathered together, not only because they did not do good, but because they left a memorial of their foolishness in the world, so that the things in which they acted wickedly could not be forgotten.
But wisdom rescues those who serve her from suffering.

Wisdom rescued righteous Jacob when he fled from the anger of his unjust brother. She led him along straight paths, showed him the kingdom of God, gave him knowledge of the truth, made his labor prosper, and enriched him through his work.
She stood by him against the oppression of his oppressors and made him wealthy.

She guarded him from his enemies and strengthened him against those who rose against him. She gave him victory in a fierce struggle, so that he might know that the fear of God is stronger than anything.
She did not abandon righteous Joseph when he was sold, but rescued him from sin.

She went down with him into the pit and did not abandon him in prison, until she gave him a royal scepter and authority over those who had overpowered him. She showed that those who accused him were liars, and she gave him everlasting glory.
She rescued a devout people and delivered a blameless race from the people who oppressed them.
She entered the soul of the Lord's servant, and he stood against fearsome kings with signs and wonders.
She gave the holy people the reward for their labor and led them through a wondrous land. She became a shelter for them by day and took the place of the shining stars by night.
She guided them through the fearsome Red Sea and led them through mighty waters.
The waters covered their enemies, and you brought them up from the depths of the abyss.
Because of this, the righteous brought trouble upon the wicked and praised your holy name, Lord, with one voice. Together they praised your mighty hand.
For wisdom opened the mouths of the mute and made the tongues of infants speak clearly.
You directed their deeds through the holy prophet.
They traveled through an uninhabited wilderness and pitched their tents where no path had been made.
They stood firm in battle and struck their enemies.
Your people grew thirsty and called to you, and you gave them water from a flint rock and relief for their thirst from solid stone.
For when they took vengeance on their enemies, they themselves were in need, and they were given what they needed.
Instead of the source of a river overflowing with blood, with red waters,
as retribution for the children who were killed by command, you gave them water with good, unending life.
Therefore you showed that it was through thirst that you exacted retribution from their adversaries.
When they were tested, and you disciplined and led them with mercy, they learned that the wicked are scourged and humiliated in wrath.
These, Father, you chose, comforted, and tested; but those you killed and condemned like an angry king.
You crushed those far away and those nearby.
Double distress seized them, along with groans at the memory of what had happened.
For they heard of their own retribution, because when things went well for them they did not acknowledge the Lord.
But they scoffed at what happened to them, and they were astonished at the outcome of their departure. Their cry was not like that of the righteous.

But just as their thoughts were without understanding, so was their wrongdoing. Because they went astray and worshiped creeping things and speechless animals, you sent many speechless animals against them as a humiliating punishment.
This was so that they would know that a person is judged and punished through the very thing by which he sins.
For you did not lack the power with which you created the world from undefined matter. You could have sent many wolves against them.
Or the fury of lions, or the terrifying flash of lightning, or the fury of many unknown beasts, or fire that blows and consumes, or the force of billowing smoke, or the power of blazing lightning.
These could not only destroy them; even the sight of them could destroy them.

Apart from all these things, you could have swept them away and destroyed them with a single breath. They could have been driven before your vengeance and scattered before the blast of your spirit. But you brought everything upon them in precise measure, order, and weight.
For great things always stand before you, and who can stand against your right arm?
For the whole created world is like the blink of an eye before you, and like dew that falls on the earth in the morning.
You have mercy on everyone, because you can accomplish everything, and you overlook people's sins when they repent.
You love everything and reject nothing that you have made, because if you had hated anything, you would not have made it.
For how could anything have endured unless you had willed it? Or how could anything have been preserved unless you had commanded it?
You spare everything, because everything belongs to you, Lord; you are the lover of souls.
For your good spirit dwells in everything.
Little by little you reprove those who stumble. You correct and rebuke them for the sins they commit, so that they may flee from evil and believe in you, Lord.
For even those who formerly lived in the holy land—
You hated them because of their filthy deeds, their acts of sorcery, and their improper rites.
They killed their children without mercy. They ate human flesh [?]. Among themselves they made an image of destruction; they performed unlawful rites in their midst.
There was no help for the lives of their people's children, and you wanted to destroy them by the hand of the fathers.
So that God's servants might receive a peaceful dwelling—the land you gave in honor and glory.
Yet you had pity even on these as human beings. You sent hornets ahead to fight, so that they might destroy them little by little.
But it was not because the wicked were too strong for the righteous to destroy them, or for them to be crushed by savage beasts or by a deadly utterance from the mouth.

Instead, you judged them little by little and gave them an opportunity to repent, because you know that their origin is evil, that their wickedness is planted within them, and that their thoughts never change.
For the offspring of sinners is cursed before the Lord. It was not because you feared sinners that you gave them more time.

For who can say to you, “What are you doing?” Or who can oppose your judgments? Who has complained about the peoples of the nations when you destroy them? Or who will stand before you demanding justice for wicked people?
For there is no other God besides you. You care for everything, and you have shown that you have judged nothing unjustly.
Neither a king nor a ruler can stand before you concerning what you have justly condemned.
You govern everything justly. And whatever deserved to be condemned to punishment, according to your power, [?] foreigners.
For your power is the source of justice. You have authority over everything, and you spare everything.
You displayed mighty deeds, and they did not believe in the power of fulfillment alone. You sternly rebuke those whom you know.
But you, Lord, have authority over power, and you judge with care. You govern us with complete mercy, for whenever you wish, power is abundant.
Through these deeds you taught your people and your children that a righteous person must love other human beings. You gave your children good hope, and you grant repentance for sins.
For you condemned even the enemies of your servants to death and afflicted them with every punishment. They asked to be given time for supplication, so that they might flee from evil.
With great care you judged them, your people and your children, for whom you made covenants, oaths, and good promises with our fathers.
You gave us a judgment by scourging those who hate us with myriads of lashes, so that when we judge, we may remember your goodness, and when we are judged, we may await your mercy.
For when they lived as fools and came to an end unjustly, you punished them through their uncleanness.
For they fled and wandered along the paths of their error, trusting in animals and in the disgrace of their enemies as gods—[?] a punishment for children, for the foolishness of their lies.
Therefore, as though they were children without understanding, you sent upon them a judgment that made them a laughingstock.
Those who do not learn from a judgment that makes them a laughingstock will taste God's judgment in earnest.

They were enraged by the very things through which they suffered, because they trusted in them as gods, and through these same things vengeance would be taken on them. For those who saw at first and denied, refusing to seek God in truth, will face the judgment held ready for them.
Human beings who do not know God are empty-headed. Even from the good things that are visible, they could not discern the One who exists. They did not look at the works or recognize their maker.
They supposed that fire, wind, light air, the revolutions of the stars, the flow of water, the lights of heaven, or the ordered structure of the world were gods.
If you suppose that they are gods because of their beauty, how much better than them is the one who made them—the one who created beauty, who made all these things!
And if they feared them because of their power and their wonderful nature, let them learn from these things that the one who made them is better than they are.
For they were created from the greatness of his beauty; the one who created them is plainly seen.
Only slight wrath will come upon these people, because perhaps they went astray while seeking God and trying to find knowledge.
They moved about among his works, becoming corrupted as they examined them, and were persuaded by appearances that what is seen is beautiful.
Yet he will not let them off at the judgment.
And if they were able to know all these things, and discovered and understood the world's structure, how did they not know and find the Lord of the whole creation?

Miserable are those whose hope is in dead things, who called the work of human hands gods: gold and silver, works of craftsmanship, likenesses of animals, and a rejected stone worked by a stonemason's hands.

Or a carpenter eagerly cut wood from a thicket, a planted tree that swayed gracefully. He carved it skillfully on every side, secured it and carved it, and carefully fashioned it into a beautiful object for use in daily life.
He used its shavings for his food needs and was satisfied, and whatever he lacked he supplied from it.

What was discarded from it was fit for nothing, and of his own devising he made a vessel suited to uncleanness. It was hard wood from a tree planted beside water and standing there. He took it and worked it diligently, and on a day when he was free he outlined it and shaped it into a human image.
Or he shaped it like a beautiful animal, coated it with pigments, painted it red, and adorned it with all the beauty found on earth.
He makes a place suited to it, sets it in the wall, and secures it with nails.
He took care that it should stand and not fall, because he knew it had no ability to help itself, since it was an image and needed a helper.
They pray to it about their plans for possessions, marriages, and children. He is not ashamed to speak with something that has no soul, and asks something sick to make him well and heal him.
For life he asks something dead to give him life. He begs something that does not know how to do him good, and asks something that cannot walk to make his paths straight.
In matters of trade in things made by hand, he makes requests of something that is useless.
Or, when he sets out to travel by ship on the sea over astonishing waves, he prays and asks a fragile piece of wood, more fragile than the ship carrying him, to help him.
The ship was made for trade; a craftsman made it with his wisdom.
But you, Father, created everything by your wisdom and your providence, and gave a road through the sea and firm paths over the waves.
to show that you can preserve life and rescue from anything, and that everything can be done with skill.

For you yourself willed and made everything, and your wisdom never ceases working. Therefore you allowed human beings to entrust their lives to a small piece of wood, and they crossed mighty waves and survived.

For from the beginning the chosen giants perished and passed away, though they had hoped to settle in the world. They fled and left the world no offspring to be born. This providence belongs to you, who created.
Blessed is the wood through which a righteous person is seen.
But what is made by human hands is cursed, both it and its maker, who made a perishable object and called it a god.
The wicked person and his wickedness are hateful to God.
The work and its maker will be condemned together.

Therefore punishment also comes upon the idols of the nations, because they are God's creation, but people made them into something defiled, a stumbling block for human souls, and traps for the feet of foolish people.
For the devising of idols is the beginning of sexual immorality, and they bring destruction to the living.
They did not exist from the beginning, nor will they remain forever.
For human gluttony entered the world; therefore the end came suddenly.

For a father took a mourning offering amid the trembling of living creatures, and his son too was to be taken away. He made an image of a human being who had then died, and now made it the likeness of a god, and gave those under his authority the mysteries of worship.
Wickedness spread and grew strong [?] time, and teaching preserved it as a law. At the command of tyrants they worshiped carved images.

Because they could not honor in person someone who lived far away, they made themselves an image of those who lived far away, a recognizable image to honor the king, so that they might entreat the distant one as though he were near, with all their natural eagerness.
The craftsman's skill encouraged even someone who did not know him to worship one who was just like himself.
For the one engaged in the work, wishing to please him, pushed his skill to produce superior beauty for him.
All the crowds rushed toward it because of the beauty of the work, and worshiped the one whom, only a little earlier, they had honored as a human being.
This became a source of ruin in life: human beings were subjected to slavery because of beauty and power, and you gave names to stones and pieces of wood that had no share in them.
It was not enough for you that you did not know God; you also waged war to make a name for evil without knowing it.
You worshiped them, killed your children, performed secret mysteries, and acted madly in other arrangements of worldly affairs.

Because of them, neither your way of life nor your marriages were pure, nor were they protected. One person treacherously killed his companion, ruined him through deceit, and ruined his fellow craftsman.
For everything was mixed together: bloodshed, murder, theft, deceit, wrongdoing, faithlessness, disorder, and false oaths. All these things are torment to those who practice them.
So that they do not remember kindness, and defile souls, and change their offspring's marriages in disorder, adultery, and impurity.
For the practices associated with their idols, whose names have perished, and their worship are the beginning of all evil.
It is a cause of corruption: if they revel, they defile themselves; if they prophesy, they lie; if they live, they act unjustly; and if they swear, they do not abandon falsehood.
For they trust in idols that are of no use, and they swear wickedly, without expecting any punishment to come from them.
Two things will certainly come upon them, because they thought wickedly about God and looked to idols, and because, contemptible as they are, they swore deceitfully and despised the truth.
This power of retribution is not because of the oaths; rather, it is punishment for the sin of sinners and condemnation of the unjust for what they have done.
But you, our God, are kind and forgiving. You are patient, your goodness is great, and you sustain everyone.
Even if we sin, we are yours, for we know your power. Yet we do not sin, because we know that we are counted as yours.
To know you is complete righteousness, and to know your truth is the root of immortality.
The work of human hands did not lead us astray: their emptiness, the shadow of their paintings, the fruitless labor of their hands, empty visions and changing images.
It is beloved in the eyes of fools, who desire dead things—a splendor with no breath in it.
They are evildoers, and those who fight over them, love them, and fear them deserve this very hope.

For look: a potter laboriously kneads soft clay and molds useful vessels from it. From the same clay he makes vessels that are clean for service and vessels that are not clean for their work. The potter himself assigns each one its use.

With wicked craftsmanship he molds a worthless god from it, though he himself was brought out of the earth only a little while ago and will shortly return to the earth, when the debt of his life is demanded of him.

He is troubled that he cannot labor, not over whether his lifetime is short or long, but over a lost lifetime of gold, silver, and bronze [?]. They imitate him, make him in impurity, and set him up in glory.
His heart is ashes, his hope is dust, and his life is dishonorable clay.
For he does not know the one who formed him, placed a complete soul within him, and breathed the spirit of life into him.
They considered the span of their lives a joke, and their life like a merchant's buying and selling, with all his trade conducted in wickedness.
He knows better than anyone that he is sinning—the one who makes carved images from earthy material and serves them.
They are all contemptible and miserable, and the enemies of your people exert their power over the life of the little one [?].

For they considered all the idols of the nations to be gods, though their eyes cannot see anything, their nostrils cannot smell the air, their ears cannot hear, the fingers of their hands cannot move, and their feet are incapable of walking.
For a human being made them, and a deceitful spirit fashioned them; none of them can make a god like a human being.
He is a mortal human being and makes dead things with sinful hands. He is better than what he worships, because he can live, but they cannot.
In their foolishness they even worship unclean animals, and these are worse than those.
They longed for the sight of animals, to receive them as good things, and turned away from God's praise and his blessing.
For this reason he took vengeance on them as they deserved, for they were scourged with every creeping and crawling creature.
You did many good things for your people. You brought them unfamiliar food to satisfy their longing, and you brought them an abundance of quail to satisfy their longing.

They longed for food, and you sent it to them, and they were changed in their desires. They asked for little, made use of food they had not known, and were strengthened. You withheld from them nothing they needed.
To those others you sent hunger and poverty because of their grumbling and their tyranny, while to these you showed that you had scourged their enemies.
You brought the venom of snakes upon them, and snakes bit them because of their transgression. But the anger did not last to the end.
Rather, they were disciplined briefly for correction, so that they would remember life through the commandment of your law.
For the one who turned back was not kept alive because he saw power, but because of you, for you are the giver of life to all.
And through these things you convinced our enemies that you are the one who saves from every evil.
For locusts and flies were biting those others, and they were dying. There was no healing for their lives, because they deserved to suffer retribution through these creatures.
But your children overcame the terror of serpents and their jaws, because you sent your grace and healed them.
So that they would remember your words, you rescued them and hurried to give them relief, so that they would not fall into the depths and forget you, since they were worthy of your good gifts.
For neither roots nor poultices healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals everyone.
For you have authority over death and life. You bring people down to the gates of Sheol and bring them up.
For a person is killed by his wickedness, and the spirit departs and does not return, nor does the soul that is taken away come back.
And no one can escape from your hands.
For you scourged the wicked who denied you with the power of your arm. You changed their rain into hailstones, pursued them with no one to rescue them, and destroyed them with fire.

In your great glory, water did not extinguish it. This was the extraordinary thing: in water, which puts out fire, the fire blazed all the more, because the whole creation helps the righteous in battle.
When you wish, the fire obeys and does not burn the animals you sent against the wicked, so that, when they saw this, they believed that they were being judged by God's judgment.
And when you wished, fire burned in water and blazed up to burn the crops of the oppressors' land.
You fed your people the food of angels and gave them bread from heaven, prepared without labor, sweeter than every sweetness and tastier than every flavor.
Through your provisions you openly gave sweetness to your children, and you served them according to their desires. It was blended for each person according to his wish.

Fire arose amid snow and ice, yet they did not melt, so that they might know that fire destroyed their enemies’ crops as it blazed amid hail and hailstones and sent out flashes of lightning in the rain.
So that the righteous might be set apart and not forget your power.
For your whole creation is subject to you. You assigned punishment to the oppressors and gave health to those who trust in you.
For this reason it changes in every way and serves your gift, which provides for each person according to his wishes.
This was to teach the children whom the Lord loves that it is not the production of crops that nourishes a person, but your word that preserves those who believe in it.
Many times fire came, and they were not harmed. Yet those things that did not melt in the fire wilted before the sun when it came with its heat.
So that they might know that even the sun stands in thanksgiving and offers it to you as its light dawns.
For the hope of the wicked melts like winter ice and is poured out like water that is thrown away.
For your judgments are great and astonishing to recount. Because of this, those who are insolent in their souls went astray.
For sinners hoped to enslave your holy people, but they reckoned themselves prisoners of darkness and counselors of the night.
They hoped to escape the thoughts of the world, and they hoped to hide their sins. They were rebuked for what they had done, scattered, terrified beyond measure, thrown into confusion, and cast down.
The darkness that seized them imprisoned them in fear. A voice of cursing met them, and suddenly their eyes grew dark, and there was no light upon them.
They were scattered by a surge of fire. Their flame was bright and did not go out, and they hoped that they would have light in the darkness of that night.
The fire alone gave them light, but they could not see its appearance. The sight they saw was terrible.
They hoped to practice the craft of sorcerers, but in their arrogant thinking they were afflicted with disgrace, stings, and terror.
Their souls were treated harshly, and they grew sick with ridicule and fear.
Every strange thing frightened them: flies in their filth and creeping things in [?]. And they fell because of birds.
They trembled and perished, and they fled from air that was nothing—unbelievers who would not believe.
For their wickedness testifies against them and condemns them for doing evil, and they clung to their own thoughts.
What is their fear but a surrender to evil and an aid to the thoughts that are within?
It expects something less than itself, yet it is greater than what it does not know, and it is the cause of the distress that comes.
The night was powerless and could not come from Sheol in its chains; in it they lay asleep.
In your sleep you saw your own soul, which you were guiding, and you blew upon everything you saw.
You appeared to be bound, though not with bonds, and you were imprisoned.
Whether you were a farmer or a shepherd, or were weary from labor in the fields, you were seized and placed in distress that you had not expected.

Darkness has one entrance, and everyone prays because of it. For they were all bound with one chain of darkness: whether it was whistling winds, the sound of the wings of birds singing sweet notes, or the sound of waters rushing violently,
or the sound of stones falling upon stones, or the sound of animals running and leaping unseen, or the sound of wild beasts roaring, or the sound of an echo among the mountains—it left them in fear.
For all creatures shine in the beauty of the light, and all his work is undisturbed.
Only over them lay a heavy night, an image of the darkness that was to come upon them. It was a heavy night for them.
But for your righteous people there was a great, shining light. They heard his voice but did not see his form, and they too were scourged and blessed.
For they admitted that they were being rightly punished, because they had been the first to oppress, and they pleaded with him.
A pillar of fire showed them the way, and you gave them honor from the heat of the sun.

Their enemies were deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness because they had kept many of your children in bondage. Through these children the light of the law was destined to shine, the law that is given without corruption to the people of their enemies.

They planned to kill the infants and the innocent, but one holy child was preserved to rebuke them, to bring about the destruction of their many children. And you destroyed the enemies of your people all together in mighty waters.
That night was known to our fathers, so that they might know with certainty in whom they had trusted for life.
You gave life to your people, the righteous, and destruction to their enemies.
You took vengeance on the enemies, and you called us, sanctified us, and glorified us.

For your devout servants worshiped secretly through your grace. Laws of truth were established together, so that the devout would share alike in good things and hardships, and from that hour would offer praise to the Father.
Unmatched distress came upon the enemies, and they mourned over the destruction of their children.
In that judgment, retribution was exacted from slave and master alike, and king and poor person suffered equally.
They all died together by the same death, and they were beyond counting. The living could not bury the dead, for in the blink of an eye their precious offspring were destroyed.
They did not believe all these things because of their sorcery, but at the destruction of their firstborn they acknowledged that the people were God’s son.
For stillness and silence held everything, and at midnight there was bewilderment.
Your almighty word came from heaven, from the throne of the wondrous kingdom, [?] warriors; in the midst of destruction it swept down upon the earth.
It brought a sharp sword at your impartial command, stood, and filled everything with the command. It reached as far as heaven and stood upon the earth.
Then suddenly visions of evil dreams disturbed them, and a fear they had not expected came upon them.
They were thrown down and fell here and there. Each of them, between death and life, showed them for what offense they were dying.
For the dreams that terrified them had warned them of this beforehand, so that they would not perish without knowing why they were suffering so terribly.
But at one time the righteous too were overtaken by a trial of death, and many perished in the wilderness. Yet your anger did not persist to the end.

For a righteous man hurried and put on the priestly garments. He went forward to fight with the weapons of his priesthood, offering supplication, prayer, and incense for atonement. He stood against the fury and turned back the anger, and the plague was stopped. Thus it became known that he was your servant.
He prevailed over the multitude, not by bodily strength or by the toil of a lifetime, but by a word he subdued the destroyer, recalling the covenants and the oaths made to the ancestors.
For when the dead had fallen in heaps, one upon another, he stood between the dead and the living. He turned back the anger and cut a path between the dead and the living.
On the [?] of his garment was the whole people, and the glory of the ancestors was engraved on four rows of stones on his shoulders. The crown of your majesty was on his head.
The destroyer obeyed these things, but they were afraid, for the trial of wrath alone was enough.
But fury without mercy stood against the wicked to the very end, for he knew beforehand even what lay ahead for them.
For they turned back so that they would be no more. They had sent them away hurriedly, but then regretted it and pursued them.

For while mourning was still on their hands and they were dancing as they buried the dead, they conceived another senseless plan. They pursued as fugitives those whom they had sent away while begging them to leave.

For retribution was dragging them toward an unavoidable end, and they did not remember what had happened to them, so that through torment they would complete this one punishment still missing from their scourges.
Your people would experience an extraordinary journey, while they would meet an unfamiliar death.
For the whole creation was being made anew according to its natural order, and in its nature it obeyed your commands, so that your servants might be kept unharmed.

A cloud overshadowed the whole camp. From the standing waters, dry ground appeared from the depths of the earth. An unobstructed road was opened through the Red Sea, and a plain full of every kind of grass met them amid the surging waters.
Through it the whole people passed, sheltered by your hand, and they saw wonders and marvels.
They grazed like horses and skipped like lambs, and they praised you, Lord, who had delivered them.

For they remembered what had happened where they had lived as foreigners: how, instead of the birth of animals, the earth brought forth creeping and swarming creatures, and instead of creatures that swarm in the water, the river poured out many frogs.
After these things, at the end, they again saw a new production of birds, when your people had first felt a craving and asked for food to sustain them.
And, as though to comfort them, you brought quails up from the sea for them.
Punishments came upon the sinners, not without preceding signs of wrath and distress. For they suffered justly for their wicked deeds, since they had devised an evil course.
Those others did not welcome people they did not know when they were there; these, however, enslaved the foreigners who had provided for them.
And not only this, but judgment will come upon them because they were unwilling to release the foreigners.
But they had joyfully welcomed those on whose account they received retribution, because they mistreated them with hard labor.

They were struck with darkness, like the people of Sodom at the righteous man's doorway, who were struck with dazzling flashes and with darkness that covered them. Each of them searched for the entrance to his own doorway.

For on their account the elements were rearranged, just as on a lyre, in the sound of melodies, the names of the notes change, while throughout it the sound remains. This is an illustration of the appearance of the things that actually happened [?].
For barren land was being turned into pools, and creeping creatures were walking on the land.
Fire blazed in water, yet did not burn with its full force, and the waters, with all their force, did not extinguish the fire.
The flame did not burn the destructive creatures or harm their flesh as they moved through it, nor did the hailstones that destroy crops melt.
For in everything, Lord, you exalted your people and glorified them. You did not abandon them in any way, but helped them everywhere and at all times.
